main_text.l: Græcii, & alibi, sunt cavernæ & carceres sub-
terranei, ad quos supernè descenditur per
cochleas. Huc conferunt, ut Virgilianus ille
cavernis ingens argentum: & sic non modo
summo cum voluntatis consensu, sed etiam
tam beata cruce, diris devoventes. Di-
vitias autem suas ita plerunque condunt,
Altari maiori & eminentiori: atque sic cum Missam
monæ sacra faciunt. In carceribus vero sub-
miseri, artuatim distrahuntur, si qui deve-
ridum manus. Non desunt tragicæ ve-
stes carnificum, pileus pyramidatus, atris plumis
ad talos usque demissæ, ut vel intuenti horrorem

page.notes: The printed catchword "pulorum" sits at the lower right. A small stray mark lies below the text block, centre, and was not transcribed. The text was read at the scan's resolution; the long s and the s/f shapes were read as plain s. Words such as "fumimo" and "confensu" were read as "summo" and "consensu" from the context of the letter shapes.
